---
title: "About This Website"
---

This website is a learning portfolio I built during the *Data Science for Psychologists* course. The work centres on the topic I study in my own research on visual attention, eye movements, and learning trajectory. Each portfolio piece develops a slightly more advanced analytical skill on top of real data rather than toy examples.

The eleven pieces form three linked mini-projects. The first analyses the OneStop eye-tracking corpus to study how word length, frequency, and contextual predictability shape reading behaviour, working up from descriptive plots to linear mixed-effects models. The second is a series of secondary analyses on a published oculomotor capture experiment (Zhang & Gaspelin, 2026, Exp. 3), asking what changes across a 3-trial sequence in measures the original paper did not test, and then zooming in on the full within-trial fixation sequence. The third is a three-stage hidden Markov model of distractor-suppression learning that ends with a cross-task transfer prediction from a Visual Search Task to an RSVP attentional blink.

The technical arc mirrors the scientific one: early pieces lean on `tidyverse`/`ggplot2` and base R workflows, the middle pieces add `lme4`/`lmerTest` for mixed-effects modelling, and the final three rely on `depmixS4` for fitting and decoding HMMs. Everything is written in R Markdown and rendered as a static website hosted on GitHub Pages.

The full source, including the rendered HTML and the supporting `.R` files where shareable, lives in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/mumizz/DS4P_Portfolio). If something looks off or you have questions about a particular piece, the repo's issues page is the best place to flag it.
